references.text: Parallel passage in Mark: Jesus rose early in the morning and went out to a deserted place to pray. The same event where Jesus withdraws to a lonely place.
Parallel passage in Mark: Simon and the others looked for Jesus and said that everyone was seeking him, corresponding to the crowd that sought after Jesus in Luke.
Jesus withdrew to a deserted place, but the crowds followed him. A recurring pattern where Jesus seeks solitude, yet the people seek him out.
Luke again tells us that Jesus withdrew to deserted places to pray, showing his habit of seeking solitude and prayer.
Jesus invited the disciples to go to a deserted place to rest, but the crowd discovered it and followed. The same pattern of withdrawal and the crowd's eagerness to find him.
The news about Jesus spread everywhere in the region, explaining why the crowds sought after him and wanted to keep him from leaving.
Jesus withdrew alone to the mountain because the crowd wanted to make him king by force. The crowd tried to hold him back, similar to the situation in Luke 4:42.
A whole crowd asked Jesus either to stay with them or leave them—showing the crowd's reactions to Jesus and their desire to control his movements.
The Lord's servant wakes up each morning to listen, just as Jesus rose early and went out to seek God's will in prayer in a lonely place.
